canonical_question: Are the 'cyan-colored isocomposition surfaces' in Fig 4H generated using a specific software algorithm or a standard statistical method?

question_variants.resolution_summary: The text mentions the existence of 'cyan-colored isocomposition surfaces' to visualize oxygen-rich regions but does not describe the specific software algorithm or statistical method used to generate them.

answers.answer: A set of cyan-colored isocomposition surfaces reveals regions containing more than 3.5 at % O. No algorithm or statistical method for their generation is described.
answers.boundary_limitation: Method of generation not specified in the provided text.
evidence_spans: For the nitrogen-doped N-2 HEA, an additional low-temperature peak (blue curve) and two high-temperature peaks (green and magenta curves) were also observed (see Fig. 5C ).
The peak height of the additional low-temperature peak is 0.002, and that of the two high-temperature peaks is 0.027 and 0.009, respectively.
Hence, only ~5.3% of all the nitrogen atoms in the N-2 HEA contribute to the formation of ordered nitrogen complexes.
